title: Lior and the Salt
premise: Gideon Joubert, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Salt Guild, which trades in impossible things — memories, debts of blood, favors owed to dead gods. When prayers begin being answered again after a century of silence, Gideon discovers the old gods are not returning but escaping: something has been wearing King Aldric's crown and feeding on his memories to keep them bound. As dragon-fire — the last flame that seals the gods' prison — gutters toward extinction, Gideon must choose between his oath to the Guild and the woman who once took his memory as payment. He unbinds Aldric by giving back what was stolen, at the cost of his own name in every ledger, and the book ends with the gods freed into a world that must learn justice without their law.
about_author: Wren Okafor is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing colonial-era debt records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ledgers, oaths, and the people history forgets to count.

chapters.title: The Weight of Salt
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the Salt Guild's counting house, Gideon audits a shipment of bottled memories and notices one vial that hums when no prayer should be answered. The emotional beat is quiet unease — a man whose whole life is order sensing something unaccounted for.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A fisherwoman's prayer for her drowned son is answered overnight; the boy returns wrong, remembering other lives. Gideon investigates and finds the seal-stone under the harbor cracked. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Searching Guild archives, Gideon finds his own name struck through in an old ledger — an entry he never made. His mentor Vess warns him to stop asking. Beat: the first crack in his trust in the Guild.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sold Yesterday
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with flashback. Isolde Marrec arrives to buy back a memory she sold years ago — the day she and Gideon loved each other, which he cannot remember. Beat: longing tangled with professional coldness; love against duty introduced.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde, now a court physician, reveals she sold that memory to fund her way into the palace — where King Aldric speaks to empty chairs and sometimes answers in a voice not his own. Beat: revelation; the two threads braid together.

chapters.title: Swordspeaking
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Attacked by Guild enforcers sent to silence him, Gideon speaks his first true word of power in years — the oath-magic he swore never to use again. Beat: reluctant power awakened; the cost is a memory burned from him.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Beneath the palace, Isolde finds the vault where the last dragon-fire gutters in its iron cradle, and the thing wearing Aldric's crown tending it like a warden. Beat: awe curdling to horror — the fire is both prison and prisoner.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon bargains with Vess for access to the sealed ledgers of the Binding, offering his swordspeaker's oath as collateral. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed; he signs away the only identity he trusts.

chapters.title: The God of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A minor god, half-freed, trades Gideon information about the Binding for a kindness — the first unpaid gift in the story. Beat: wonder returning; the world is stranger and kinder than the ledgers say.

chapters.title: Ash on the Water
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The crown-thing purges the palace; loyal servants are emptied and refilled with devotion. Isolde escapes with proof and a burn scar shaped like a crown. Beat: terror and resolve; stakes become bodily.

chapters.title: The Broken Oath Road
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Fleeing the Guild, Gideon travels the old oath-road with the fisherwoman's returned son as guide — a boy who remembers the Binding from a life before his own. Beat: found-family warmth amid pursuit.

chapters.title: Vess's Confession
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess reveals the Guild was founded by theBinding's architects to administer the gods' debts — and that Gideon's name was struck because he was promised to the fire as a child. Beat: betrayal reframed as protection; grief.

chapters.title: What Isolde Bought
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde finally opens the vial of her own memory and remembers loving Gideon — and remembers that he asked her to sell it, to save him from the Guild's notice. Beat: heartbreak inverted; love proven by absence.

chapters.title: The Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The crown-thing offers Gideon a trade: Aldric's freedom for the return of all stolen god-memories, knowing the flood will drown mortal minds. Beat: temptation; justice outside the law means no clean options.

chapters.title: Riot of the Unremembered
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The city erupts as half-returned memories drive crowds mad with borrowed grief. Gideon chooses to stand between mob and palace rather than fight either. Beat: moral climax approaching; courage without violence.

chapters.title: Into the Iron Cradle
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Guided by the boy and armed with Isolde's knowledge of the vault, Gideon descends past the dying fire while Guild enforcers and crown-devoted battle above. Beat: descent, literal and moral; fear mastered.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing Him
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Face to face with the warden, Gideon learns it is the first king — Aldric's ancestor — who bound the gods to stop their justice and became the binding himself. Beat: pity for the monster; the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Gideon and Isolde's alternating POV. Gideon speaks the unbinding word, paying with every ledger-entry of his name; Isolde holds Aldric's mind steady as his stolen years pour back. Beat: climax — love and sacrifice fused; the fire flares white.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Gods
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The gods walk free into a world with no law for them; Aldric, restored and diminished, abdicates to a council. Isolde searches the ashes for a man no ledger can name. Beat: exhaustion, hope, uncertainty.

chapters.title: The Man Without Entries
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Nameless, Gideon wanders the city unrecognized — free and unbearably light. The fisherwoman's son calls him by a name the boy invented for him. Beat: identity rebuilt from relationships, not records.

chapters.title: Salt and Bread
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Gideon and Isolde meet as strangers who are not strangers; she offers him bread and the memory of their day, spoken aloud since he cannot hold it. Beat: tender resolution; love chosen anew without the crutch of memory.

chapters.title: The First Unpaid Gift
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, epilogue. The new council asks Gideon to build a justice that needs neither gods nor ledgers; he opens a small school where children learn to speak oaths they can keep. The last line echoes the first vial's hum. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
